Here is a comprehensive overview of everything you should know about the Swedish javelin thrower, Mats Nilsson. ### **Introduction: Who is Mats Nilsson?** Mats Nilsson (born 17 June 1969) is a retired Swedish track and field athlete who specialized in the javelin throw. He was one of the world's elite throwers during the 1990s, a highly competitive era for the event. While he didn't win a global championship gold medal, he is best remembered for his immense throwing power and for setting the **Swedish national record** that still stands today. --- ### **Key Career Highlights and Achievements** Nilsson was a consistent performer who regularly qualified for the finals of major international championships. * **1991 World Championships (Tokyo):** Finished 8th with a throw of 78.50 m. * **1993 World Championships (Stuttgart):** Finished 8th again, this time with a throw of 78.56 m. * **1994 European Championships (Helsinki):** This was arguably his best championship performance. He finished in **4th place**, just missing out on a medal with a throw of 80.80 m. * **1995 World Championships (Gothenburg):** Competing on home soil, there were high hopes for Nilsson. In a major disappointment, he failed to qualify for the final, finishing 15th in the qualifying round. * **1996 Olympic Games (Atlanta):** He made it to the Olympic final, ultimately finishing in **10th place** with a throw of 80.84 m. He was also a multiple-time Swedish national champion in the javelin throw. --- ### **The National Record and Personal Best** The crowning achievement of Mats Nilsson's career is his **personal best throw of 89.10 meters**. * **Date:** 27 July 1995 * **Location:** The prestigious Bislett Games in Oslo, Norway. * **Significance:** This throw established a new **Swedish national record**, a mark that has not been broken since. It remains one of the longest throws in the history of the sport with the new specification javelin (implemented in 1986). At the time of this throw, it placed him among the top 10 throwers of all time. --- ### **Context of His Era: A Golden Age for Javelin** To fully appreciate Mats Nilsson's career, it's essential to understand the context of the 1990s. He competed against some of the greatest javelin throwers in history, including: * **Jan Železný (Czech Republic):** The undisputed GOAT (Greatest Of All Time), who set the world record (98.48 m) and won three Olympic gold medals. * **Steve Backley (Great Britain):** A dominant force who won multiple European championships and held the world record. * **Seppo Räty (Finland):** A fierce competitor and multiple-time world champion. * **Aki Parviainen (Finland):** Another Finn who would go on to win a World Championship. Nilsson's ability to consistently make finals and throw over 85 meters in this era cemented his status as a world-class athlete. ### **The Swedish Javelin Scene** Nilsson was also part of a strong Swedish javelin duo alongside **Patrik Bodén**. Bodén briefly held the world record in 1990 with a throw of 89.10 meters—coincidentally the exact same distance as Nilsson's later personal best. Together, Nilsson and Bodén represented a golden era for the javelin in Sweden, pushing each other to world-class results. --- ### **Summary Table** | Category | Information | | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Full Name** | Mats Nilsson | | **Nationality** | Swedish | | **Discipline** | Javelin Throw | | **Born** | 17 June 1969 | | **Personal Best** | **89.10 m** (Oslo, 1995) | | **Major Record** | Current Swedish National Record Holder | | **Key Achievements** | • 4th, 1994 European Championships
